EXAMPLE: NOT A REAL CONTRACT. The DEV-only AWS CDK pilot (one stack, one account, DEV only). Copy to config/act-pilot-contract.json, replace the fake account id and every REPLACE-WITH value with an owner-supplied value, and set enabled to true and add an authorize entry (for example {"DEV": ["APPLY", "CLEANUP"]}) only when the owner authorizes the pilot, in one reviewed commit of the contract (an absent or empty authorize keeps ACT disabled; there is no hash file). The backend is the CloudFormation stack name. The capabilities list is empty, so a stack with IAM resources needs an explicit owner decision (CAPABILITY_IAM or CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM). The pilot's cleanup never deletes the stack and refuses to leave it with no resource (CLEANUP_WOULD_EMPTY_STACK), so the stack and the canary's last resource stay, and the owner records them as a retained-resource disposition (docs/act-pilot-apply.md, CDK). There is no stack-delete authority. The account id is obviously fake and the approver placeholders are deliberately invalid, so this file can never enable ACT.
